title: What happens internally when a Java object is created
answer: For a normal `new` expression, the JVM ensures the class is loaded and initialized as required, allocates memory for the object, initializes instance fields to default values, executes instance field initializers and initialization blocks in language-defined order, invokes the selected constructor with superclass construction occurring first, and finally returns a reference to the initialized object. Exact allocation details such as TLAB use are JVM implementation details, so interview answers should separate language/JVM guarantees from HotSpot-specific optimizations.
